verification.caveat: The tree these commands ran on had uncommitted or untracked files, so no commit named here is that tree, and checking out the commit it sat on would run them on a different one. The steps look for a commit whose tree is `38a531b9b75f7dd64539533f2f8d5a5b4a73f15a` (the working-tree digest); if none has it, the checked tree was never committed and cannot be re-run from the repository. This repository has no remote configured, so this commit is reachable only where it was made.

predicate.limits: This is evidence that these commands ended as recorded against the working tree it names. It is not evidence that the work is correct, that the commands check the right things, or that the specification was satisfied. The commands ran code in this tree, including tests and build scripts the change may have edited; the tree was the same before and after the run, which cannot see an edit reverted during the run. The base checks put the base's tests back to see whether they still pass, and their runs are observed beside this evidence, never part of it. It is unsigned and detects change rather than forgery.
